sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.8% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, reaching $31.7 billion [F198][F9].
Operating income grew faster, a 5.8% CAGR to $8.6 billion, so operating margin rose from 22.9% to 27.2% [F199][F19][F20][F28].
FY2022 was the step change, revenue up 17.1% on rate cases, favorable weather and volumes [D239][P26].
FY2020 was the trough, net income down 63.3% on coal ash settlement impairments and pandemic volume losses [D157][P60].
Electric Utilities and Infrastructure supplied 90.9% of FY2025 revenue and added 3.6pp of the 5.6% growth [D541][D543][D358].
Residential electric was the largest customer class at 43.3% of revenue, contributing 2.8pp in FY2025 [D774][D776].
Gas Utilities and Infrastructure grew 27.1% and added 2.0pp, with Piedmont Natural Gas up 32.1% for 1.7pp [D565][D566][D682][D683].
Operating income grew 8.8% against 5.6% revenue growth, an incremental margin of 41.4% [D359][D358][D378].
Diluted EPS rose 10.5% against 9.8% net income growth as the share count rose 0.6% [D362][D360][D374].
FY2025 operating margin of 27.2% is the window high, 4.3pp above the 22.9% median and 7.5pp above the FY2020 low [F28][D932][D933][D931].
Revenue grew 5.6% against 5.3% operating-cost growth, a thin 0.3pp spread that still lifted margin 0.8pp [D358][D372][D379][D370].
D&A rose to 24.3% of revenue from 21.4%, while capex ran at 44.2% of revenue [D341][D303][D342].
Net margin of 15.7% sits below the 17.6% peer median, a 25th-percentile result [F47][D952][D951].
Interest expense of $3.6 billion and an 11.2% effective tax rate kept net margin 11.5pp under operating margin [X63][D345][F47][F28].
Operating cash flow of $12.3 billion was 2.48x net income, in line with the 2.19x to 3.48x range since FY2019 [F77][F38][D346][D97][D268].
Free cash flow was negative $1.7 billion, a -5.3% margin, because capex of $14.0 billion exceeded operating cash flow [F97][D343][F87][F77].
Capex ran at 1.82x D&A, below the 2.15x FY2019 peak but still double depreciation [D348][D99].
FY2022 operating cash flow fell 28.5% as rising fuel costs created undercollections financed with borrowings [D244][P36].
Net debt reached $89.6 billion, or 282.3% of revenue, a 25th-percentile position against utilities peers [D352][D353][D953].
Total debt grew 6.6% in FY2025 while cash fell 22.0% to $245 million, and the current ratio dropped to 0.55x [D376][D366][F137][F177].
Return on average equity of 9.7% ranks at the 0th percentile against a 12.6% peer median [D357][D955][D956].
Dividends of $3.2 billion in FY2022 were funded alongside $11.9 billion of debt issued, and the diluted share count rose 4.2% in FY2021 [D234][X130][D214].
The current ratio fell to 0.55x in FY2025, below the 0.66x window median and near the 0.53x FY2020 low [F177][D945][D943].
Cash of $245 million covers 0.1 years of the latest $1.7 billion burn, leaving little buffer [F137][D356][F97].
Net cash has fallen for nine straight years, from -$50.0 billion in FY2016 to -$89.6 billion in FY2025 [D14][D352][R3].
Free cash flow was below 80% of net income in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, at -0.96x, 0.01x and -0.34x [D269][D309][D347][R4].
FY2021 operating expenses, pretax income and tax were later restated, so FY2021 comparisons carry a recast caveat [X29][X69][X79][R6].
If FY2026 operating margin holds above the 22.9% window median, the margin expansion is durable; a drop toward the 19.7% FY2020 low would reverse it [D933][D931].
Watch free cash flow margin against the -5.8% median; a return to the 0.2% FY2024 high would signal capex relief [D939][D938].
Watch the current ratio against 0.55x; a further decline below the 0.53x FY2020 low would tighten liquidity [F177][D943].
